title: Manila and vicinity, February 1899: a WarMapper reconstruction
label: 1899 (reconstructed)
about: This is a WarMapper reconstruction, not a period map. It is drawn by this page, live, from lines read off two Army maps of February 1899 and, south of Malate, a War Department plan of 1898, in the manner of a map of the time. The shore is the shore of 1899: most of today's bay front was reclaimed later. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.
notes: Proof of concept. North of the Pasig and in the city the lines come from the engineer map (S78), tied to today's ground to about 20-30 m (weaker at Caloocan). From Malate to Pasay the shore, Calle Real, blockhouses 13 and 14 and the plan's own lines come from the War Department plan of 1898 (S79), slid to today's streets and good to about 100 m; that is the ground of 1898. South of Pasay, and the Pasig above Santa Ana, are still from the Signal Corps map (S64) and may be 200-400 m out. Second pass, 21 Nov 2026: the engineer map's own street, block, dyke and field lines and its esteros were added by program. They give the city and the country their detail, but nobody has checked them line by line.
credit: WarMapper reconstruction from Haan, 1899 (National Archives), "Manila y sus arrabales", 1898 (Yale) and Warking, 1899 (Library of Congress)
